title: Can Cause Raised Itchy Bumps
body: My husband gave me this for my birthday. It seems to work great to create longer term hair loss. However, the skin irritation is massive. When I started using it I did not really consider how laser hair treatment worked. Now, after searching for my symptoms, I get it. The laser damages the hair follicle. For some people (me), the follicle then gets inflamed, fills with fluid, creates a histamine response. The result is huge itchy, sore red bumps all over the treated area. And this response is fairly common. For me, the bumps are itchy for about 4-5 days. Then the red spots last several more days til they fade. I don't treat an area again until it's healed. Otherwise, there is no real pain with use. The good is that I know it's working to get rid of the hair follicles. The bad is that each treatment results in about a week of pretty bad irritation and another week of discoloration. The itch is insane. I'm going to try to continue treating and see how long the hair loss lasts. I'm not sure it's worth it to me to continue use, but it definitely works. I still give it 4 stars because if I didn't have this histamine response it would be an absolutely fantastic product.

body: Buying this device has been a huge quality of life improvement for me. I have fair skin and thick, dark body hair all over my arms, legs, toes, etc. I used to get severe razor burn shaving my thighs, no matter WHAT I tried—and I tried everything. I bought this out of desperation, and to my delight, after a year of weekly sessions all over my entire body, I’m almost completely hairless. There are some patchy areas around my body that stubbornly refuse to get zapped, but I went from needing to shave daily to shaving once every other week max, and only before my sessions (which I’ve reduced to biweekly). However, the design of this device really needs some work. It can be REALLY hard to get the sensors to flash, even when the plate is flush against my skin. This significantly slows down the process, and doing my entire body (arms, legs, armpits, chin, belly button/happy trail, bikini area) takes TWO HOURS. I’ve managed to get it down to about an hour with less hair and better skill, but this is still WAY to arduous, and it’s entirely because of the overly cautious safety feature. I keep my eyes closed and turn my head away the entire time I do this, so for me, the extra caution is just wasting my time. Frankly, no one should be looking at the machine when it flashes to begin with, and yet, even with the safety feature, I’ve had this stupid thing flash OFF THE SKIN on accident before. So, basically, it’s a big waste of time, and it doesn’t work properly anyway. The design is also soooo uncomfortable to use at certain angles. The curve really makes it hard to get the backs of my thighs without the cord getting all tangled up. That being said, I’m grateful for this machine. I probably won’t rebuy this model when I run out of flashes, but I will continue to use at home ipl devices!

body: This is my personal experience w this item. I bought this item hoping to minimize shaving, especially during the summer. I waited about a week and a half between sessions, and noticed there was considerably less hair than before. After two sessions, it was almost gone. I waited almost three weeks before my third session and only very fine hair was left. In this sense, I was very impressed, considering I was planning on it taking months (in which case I would’ve returned the item and just gone back to get it professionally done again). Ok, now the bad: first use was ok. Was not as quick as one would imagine. I would guess (should’ve timed) it took about three hours in all kind of odd positions to do my legs, underarms, and bikini area. I was honestly hoping for something a little quicker (with that said, second session was a little faster). I also got a terrible case of follicular something or other on my lower legs during session two. It looked terrible and itched worse. That lasted about 2 weeks and left some hyper pigmented areas (these are fading and I expect them to be gone in another week). The smell of burning hair isn’t the best and you really should make sure you follow the direction on starting at the lowest setting bc I did burn myself once using too high of a setting. With all that being said, I would recommend this product. It’s not the products fault that I was sensitive to the laser or that I did not follow directions on laser strength. quote: since bright lights can give me migraines, I have to be careful
title: Finally Winning the Neck Hair Battle
body: I’ve been using this Braun IPL weekly for a little over two months now, mostly on my neck and upper lip. I was blessed (or cursed) with the neck hair and peach fuzz of a teenage boy, and I used to spend way too much time plucking or secretly shaving. For the first part of my relationship, I even hid that I shaved my neck, though when I finally admitted it my partner didn’t care at all. Still, it has been a huge source of embarrassment for me since my early 20s. I thought about paying a fortune for professional laser treatments, but I decided to give this a try instead. And honestly, I’m glad I did. The hair is already growing much slower, and for the first time I have real hope it might stop completely. It doesn’t hurt, especially if you’re used to plucking, and it’s easy to switch between the larger and smaller attachments. The pouch it comes with is actually cute and practical, and everything fits inside neatly. I like that it also came with a razor and clear instructions. I use it at the highest power setting, and it hasn’t overheated or smelled weird, though I’m only treating a small area. My only real complaint is the lack of eye protection. I have to cover my eyes with my hand, which means I can’t see what I’m doing. Even with that, the flash of light is still visible and since bright lights can give me migraines, I have to be careful. So far it’s been fine, but I really wish it came with glasses or some sort of shield. And a heads-up: don’t use it on moles, unshaved hair, or darker skin tones, according to the manual. It also isn’t recommended for light hair, and it may not work as well for hormonal hair like PCOS. Overall, it’s a great option if you have lighter skin and darker hair and want to start zapping away unwanted growth without breaking the bank. For me, it’s a solid 4 out of 5 stars and a small but satisfying victory in the long war against neck/facial hair.

quote: it actually burned my leg to the point that I had red rectangular spots
title: General advice + testimonial from tan skin tone
body: First off: I am a light brown skin tone in the winter, medium brown in the summer. My hair is dark. This device can definitely be effective on these skin tones. However, if your hair is thick, it will be an uphill battle. I pretty much exclusively use the device on the highest setting because I want results quickly. BUT BEWARE: after about a year of using it for a few months on and few months off, I got impatient and started clicking the button 2-3 times on each spot to really zap the follicle. This was a huge mistake. Besides the sting, it actually burned my leg to the point that I had red rectangular spots the same size and shape of the device head, and my skin peeled off the next day. DO NOT DO THIS. Also make sure you get a nice close shave before using this. I don't think there's a big risk if you don't, but it's wasted effort since you're not targeting the follicle as effectively. I was most diligent about my legs, planning to get to the rest of my body next if it worked well. I highly recommend being diligent about doing it every week. If you skip too many weeks, you may have to restart and it sucks. This device also hurts a LOT more on sensitive areas like the upper thigh and armpit, basically anywhere with sensitive skin. I found that armpit is extremely stubborn because that has thicker hair (and maybe because it hurts too much for me to really zap it a lot). But like others have said, the sting is temporary (...don't burn yourself). I really, really despise the "continuous flash" setting when you hold down the button. It's not really continuous enough to be convenient. Takes 2 seconds between each flash and it's kind of unpredictable when the sensor is finicky so you can't maintain a smooth glide. I now use the single flash (one tap of the button) every time. I also look away while it flashes if I can. Can't be good for the eyes, though I don't necessarily think it will do permanent damage?

quote: by the next day it was clear my legs were covered in 1st degree burns
title: Beware: Burns as Safety Mechanism Fails on Darker Skin Tones
body: A year ago I underwent 8 sessions of laser hair removal using the Nd Yag laser, as my skin tone is between Fitzpatrick 4 and 5 with near black hair color (for reference, closer to Rhianna's skin tone vs. Michelle Obama with hair that is 1B using synthetic hair). The sessions definitely helped reduce my growth and I never had issues with burns or skin discoloration post-procedure, but after a year I noticed more growth coming back, so I sought out at-home devices hoping to find a more affordable way to obtain a reduction in hair growth and be able to perform maintanence treatments as needed. Given my darker skin tone, I did my research and purposely sought out brands that were safer for darker skin and had built-in technology for safety. Therefore, when I came across Braun, I thought I hit the jackpot; a well-known, reputable brand that had finally updated to include technology safer to use on darker skin, and would sample my skin tone multiple times each second to ensure there was enough color difference between my hair and skin to apply a flash safely. When I received the device, I tested it across multiple areas on my body, and I definitely appreciated when it would consistently refuse to flash when I placed it over areas I suspected would be too dark to treat (e.g. my knees and over old, hyperpigmented scars). When I didn't see a reaction after 48 hours, I first treated my arms, which were slightly darker than my legs, and had no issues. Therefore, the next day I proceeded to treat my legs, confidently thinking it would be OK after the patch tests on my legs were ok, and my arm treatment had went well. Well, my first sign should have honestly been the weird, intermittent safe-unsafe signals the device kept giving, but I assumed this was because the device is really strict about having the treatment window completely covered before it will flash. Therefore, I simply would tilt my hand assuming I wasn't holding the device properly enough to cover the flash window. Well, 5 minutes into my treatment my skin started burning. I immediately stopped and cooled the area, doing my best to calm the skin without aggresively cooling it, assuming it might be burn injuries, and yep, by the next day it was clear my legs were covered in 1st degree burns. I write this review for all my tan/darker folks hoping that this device might be safe for them, and trusting that the built-in safety mechanism will protect them-- well it didn't protect me, and now I'm seeking out treatment from my dermatologist to hopefully minimize long-term scarring and hyperpigmentation. Although, weirdly, my arms are still Ok. So I suspect perhaps the device accidentally occasionally allowed too high of a treatment setting on my legs vs. my arms, given my arms are actually slightly darker with less coarse/possibly lighter hair, and the burns on my legs are patchwork and don't cover every area treated. As a result, I don't think this was a case where the skin in the treated area was too dark or didn't have enough contrast between hair and skin color, but rather, I believe the safety adjustment failed to occur. So if you are darker, keep this in mind and use this device at your own risk.

There is some negligible hair regrowth. One thing I forgot to mention in my initial review is the Ulike skin sensor is more forgiving on curved areas (like shins and ankles) than INIA. While that makes it easier to use, it also makes it a bit less safe because IPL escapes the edges of the device and treats unintended areas. Make sure you are wearing the glasses to protect your eyes. The INIA won’t fire unless the entire window is covered with skin. Both are excellent devices though. If you want a good IPL at a less expensive price, INIA. If you want a bit higher quality and don’t mind unintended treatment of areas where IPL escapes, Ulike. If I had to choose between the two, it would be difficult because I like them both. PS: be on the lookout, I received a Braun IPL to test and review and I will be comparing it to these two. Original review: This is the third IPL I have ordered. I’m going to compare this IPL with the other two. My first IPL is by INIA and it is phenomenal so Ulike has a high bar. The second one I ordered was junk and last I checked had been removed by the seller so I won’t waste your time with info on it. I’ll just say it did not work. The competition between it and INIA was hands down, INIA. Ulike IPL is a fair rival to the INIA. It comes with a very nice case to store everything in. Off the bat, it is one advantage over INIA. The quality of Ulike is superb. I like the double flash it provides, and it makes me feel like it is stronger than the INIA. It’s construction feels solid and if very good quality. When I first used my INIA, that’s what I do (bikini mode and highest setting combined) I used it daily because I knew I’d be away for 10 days and unable to use it. I had ZERO hair regrowth in that period. I’m hopeful Ulike will be the same. One big difference I noticed between INIA and Ulike is INIA’s maintenance schedule is once per year as opposed to Ulike’s which is every two weeks- to me, that is not permanent hair removal.
